item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission completed a final review of WA Police’s response to two earlier recommendations about deploying police dogs.
item.support:
provided a list of completed actions in addressing the 
Commission's two recommendations.

item.text: The review examined canine policies and oversight, and research into the disproportionate deployment of dogs on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people.
item.support:
WA Police undertake further analysis of police dog use to explore and address 
reasons for the higher representation

item.text: The Commission concluded that revised policies and procedures reduced ambiguity and risk and improved accountability for dog deployments.
item.support:
The written standards provide a framework for officer accountability and enable internal 
and external parties to oversee and/or investigate police dog deployment incidents.

item.text: The Commission closed both recommendations as appropriately addressed, while noting that incomplete data limited analysis of disproportionate deployment.
item.support:
While data constraints limited further review, the Commission acknowledges the actions 
taken by WA Police to integrate culturally sensitive practices into policy and procedures.

item.quote:
The Commission considers that WA Police appropriately responded to recommendation 
one, and it is deemed closed.

The Commission considers that WA Police responded appropriately to recommendation 
two, and it is deemed closed.
